title: Cartesia Pricing: Plans, Credits and Limits (2026)
summary: Cartesia pricing includes multiple plans with varying costs. Compare each tier's features and pricing to determine which one fits your budget and needs.
body_markdown:
## Connecting Cartesia to business workflows with Activepieces


Don't expect[Activepieces](https://www.activepieces.com/pricing) to make Cartesia cheaper: it's an automation builder with 746 integrations and an MIT-licensed core, and if an integration you need doesn't exist, you can generate one with AI and add it privately to your own instance, while a run costs 1 credit however many steps it has, so step count doesn't affect the per-run cost.


### When a workflow tool is worth adding


Add it only if speech must be generated in response to events in other tools: a form submission, a new spreadsheet row, a support ticket. Each of those needs something to notice the event and send a text-to-speech request.


If your own application already calls Cartesia directly, a workflow tool adds a second system to maintain and changes nothing about the bill. Skip it.


In the screenshot, a workflow titled "CV Scanning" has five steps, which is the kind of flow where it fits. A Web Form trigger labeled "Human Input" starts it.


Then Google Sheets logs a row, a step extracts text from a PDF, a text AI step summarizes it, and a second Sheets step writes the result back.


With the Web Form step open, you can see that the trigger gives you a published form URL and a draft one, plus a warning about "Wait for Response". Nothing in this flow produces audio.


Replace the summary step with an HTTP request to Cartesia and the same shape would turn each submission into a spoken summary. That HTTP step is where credits start being spent, so it's the step to price.


The number of flows around it is not a cost: the Activepieces pricing page lists "unlimited flows" on every tier from Free ($0, 1,000 credits a month) through Ultimate, whereas Zapier's pricing page bills a task per action and Make's bills a credit per module.


Break the fragile mega-flow into ten small ones and the only meter left running is Cartesia's credits per request.


### Keeping credit use predictable


Every trigger fire becomes a paid request unless you stop it. A spreadsheet that gets bulk-pasted, or a form that gets spammed, could send hundreds of speech requests you never intended, and each draws on your credit balance.


On the Activepieces side that burst is cheap to absorb: a run is 1 credit however many steps it has, against the Free plan's 1,000 credits a month, and if those run out the flows stay on while runs wait for the credits to refresh.


The meter to watch is the Cartesia request each run makes.


Three habits keep the spend readable:


1. Put a filter step before the HTTP call so only rows that need audio reach it.
2. Cap concurrent runs below your plan's concurrency limit.
3. Have the flow write each request's character count to a sheet, so you can compare real credit use against your estimate.
